cards.title: An approval pins the draft it saw: case and rehearsal run from one snapshot

cards.body:
## Summary
A brief and the slots and answers it was drafted from become one immutable Draft, recorded when the brief is written. Approving rev N binds that Draft: the case file and the rehearsal are built from it, never from whatever the live session holds when they happen to run.

## Description
The studio's law is draft-preview-apply (loop.py:27): what is approved is exactly what was shown. The rev check enforces that for the Brief object only. Everything around it is read live: CaseBook.save takes session.slots and session.answers at request time (cases.py:332), and the showcase takes session.brief and session.slots when its background thread gets round to them (showcase.py:684, 696). Research lanes run beside the conversation for up to 4.5 minutes (accounts up to 9) and apply findings whenever they finish (lanes.py:146); a dropped document does the same. None of that marks the brief stale (session.py:293). So a person approves a brief that says 'Deposit: not known yet' and the case file records '$1,500' under that approval; on reopen it comes back as source 'memory' (cases.py:258). An answer typed after approving drafts rev 2, and a rehearsal that has not started yet shapes rev 2's world. This is resume-after-decision's 're-generation after approval' defect (hitl-approval): the approval pinned a rev number, not the artifact.

The move: session.py gains a frozen Draft(rev, brief, slots, answers) and a small rev -> Draft map. loop._write_brief and sessions.reopen record one. loop.approve resolves the Draft for the rev it accepts. CaseBook.save(session, rev) and Showcase.run(session, rev) take session.draft_of(rev) and stop reading live state. Late findings stay on the live slots and reach the next draft (case 7), so nothing is lost and nothing unseen is approved. The hook signatures, the wire contract and the case file's shape stay the same.

## Flow
- _write_brief: snapshot slots and answers, draft, record Draft(rev, brief, slots, answers)
- reopen: record the case's approved brief as Draft(approved_rev, ...)
- approve(rev): unchanged refusals; on success the Draft for rev is the one approved
- save(session, rev) / Showcase.run(session, rev): read the approved Draft only

## Expected impact
A whole class of 'approved X, saved or rehearsed Y' defects closes: what the case file records and what the rehearsal plays are, byte for byte, what the person approved. Measured by cases 1-3.

## Evaluation
Claim: the case file and the rehearsal are built from the approved draft, never from slots or a brief that changed after it was shown.
Before: 0 of 3 behaviour cases pass (1, 2, 3); guards 4-7 green
After: 7 of 7
Method: gate - the acceptance cases
Result: better
Gate: none

Lane budgets: research.py:72 ACCOUNTS_TIMEOUT_S = 540 s, research.py:314 rules 270 s.

cards.title: A yearly chore's suggested cadence lands before her deadline, not a year out
shared_surfaces: docs/adr/0131-a-chore-comes-due-as-a-staged-review.md (amend decision 4's suggestion rule: anchored to a dated line of the approved case when one exists)
acceptance: 1. suggest_for_case(times_per_year=1, brief_md with '**Dates that matter:**\n- Protest deadline: May 15, 2026 (Texas Tax Code). If missed: ...', slots=(), today=2026-10-25) -> CadenceRule(kind='every_days', every_days=365, start='2027-05-01', at='09:00'), and the basis names 'Protest deadline', 'May 15' and that it comes due two weeks before
2. The same case with today=2026-03-01 -> start '2026-05-01' (this year's date is still ahead)
3. The same case with today=2026-05-10 (inside the two weeks) -> start '2026-05-11', basis still says it comes due before May 15
4. Two dated lines (June 30 and May 15), today=2026-10-25 -> anchored on May 15, the first that comes round
5. A brief whose dates name only a rule ('30 days after the notice arrives') -> the rule equals cad.suggest(1, today)[0] and the basis adds that the brief names no calendar date (unchanged rule)
6. times_per_year 12, 52 and None with the same dated brief -> exactly what cad.suggest returns today (unchanged)
7. No dated brief line but a confirmed fact slot 'Notice date' = '2026-04-20', today=2026-10-25 -> start '2027-04-06', basis names the notice date from her case

8. GET /adopt/cases/<proj>/cadence on a saved case whose approved brief carries the May 15 line, with no cadence set and the clock at 2026-10-25 -> reply.suggested.start == '2027-05-01' and reply.suggested_basis names the deadline (ChoreClock with a fake clock, no model)

Nothing is written to a cadence file by a suggestion, so no stored data moves.

cards.body:
## Summary
When she sets up a yearly chore, the Due panel suggests a cadence that comes due two weeks before the date her own approved brief names (her protest deadline, her notice date). Today it suggests 'every 365 days from today', which for a chore adopted after its window means it comes due after the deadline has passed.

## Description
43 of the 95 playbooks say economics.times_per_year = 1. For all of them cadence.suggest (cadence.py:265) proposes every_days = 365 starting a year from today. A property-tax protest adopted in October therefore comes due next October, months after the May window closes (UAT 2026-10-23 finding 10, backlog B-C8). The app already has the date. Each approved brief carries 'Dates that matter' (loop.py:604), written per deadline as 'what: when (rule). If missed: ...', and saved verbatim in the case file. Fact slots that name a date are already told apart (cases.py:106 perishable). The decision is made blind while the data sits in the same file the route has just loaded (chores.py:541).

The change: a pure cadence.suggest_for_case(times_per_year, brief_md, slots, today). For a chore that comes round once or twice a year, it reads the calendar dates in the brief's 'Dates that matter' lines and in her confirmed date facts. It accepts 'May 15', '15 May', 'May 15, 2026' and ISO dates. A date that names only a rule ('30 days after the notice') is not an anchor. The function takes the first month and day that comes round after today and suggests every round(365/count) days, starting 14 days before that date (tomorrow when it is closer than that). The basis is worded to read after the panel's 'because': 'your brief's Protest deadline falls on May 15, so it comes due two weeks before'. Every other chore, and a yearly one with no calendar date, gets exactly today's suggestion, and the basis says why (cases 5 and 6). A suggestion is still written nowhere until she presses 'Use the suggestion' (ADR 0131). An every_days rule of 365 drifts one day per leap year, and the 14-day lead absorbs that for over a decade. A true 'yearly' rule kind would change the contract and is left out.

## Flow
- Due panel opens a case with no cadence -> GET /adopt/cases/<proj>/cadence
- _cadence_reply -> suggest_for_case(times, case.brief_md, case.slots, today)
- the panel shows 'Suggested: every 365 days at 09:00, counted from 2027-05-01, because your brief's Protest deadline falls on May 15...' -> one press uses it

## Expected impact
For the 43 yearly playbooks, a person whose brief carries a calendar date gets a first review two weeks before that date, not up to a year late. B-C8's acceptance ('a property-tax chore adopted in October comes due before the protest window') becomes a test (cases 1 and 8).

## Evaluation
Claim: a yearly chore's suggested cadence is anchored to the calendar date in her own approved case.
Before: 0 of 6 behaviour cases pass (1, 2, 3, 4, 7, 8); guards 5-6 green
After: 8 of 8
Method: gate - the acceptance cases
Result: better
Gate: none

Suggested: ${reply.suggested_text}, because ${reply.suggested_basis}.`
